title: Why Can't Penguins Fly? 🐧 Fun Facts for Kids
description:
Penguins DO fly... underwater! Leo asks, big sister Mia explains flipper wings and heavy bones, in under a minute.

Curio Kids Club: short, curious answers to kids' big questions. Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@CurioKidsClub

lines.text: Penguins do fly... underwater! Their wings are stiff, flat flippers, perfect for zooming through the sea.
So why can't the flippers flap in the air?
Flying in the air takes big, light wings. Penguin wings are short and strong, great for pushing water, but too small to lift a penguin.
For their size, yes! They have solid, heavy bones, and most flying birds have light ones. Heavy bones help penguins dive deep.
Scientists think penguins' great-great-great grandparents, long, long ago, could fly. Over time, their wings changed to be better for swimming.
So they swapped flying for swimming!
Yes! And they're amazing swimmers. They can zip, twist, and even leap out of the water like dolphins.
On land, they waddle, hop, or slide on their tummies across the ice!
Flipper wings, heavy bones and super swimming. Penguins are awesome!
They really are! Follow Curio Kids Club for more wonders. And next time someone asks... why can't penguins fly?
